title: Understanding Voter Fraud Misinformation Videos during the 2024 Taiwan Election on YouTube
screen_reason: A content analysis with a full numerator and denominator: 170 of 5,641 YouTube videos published by 94 party-aligned Taiwanese channels between 12 Jan and 1 Feb 2024 were coded as containing the voter-fraud narrative. HOWEVER the numerator is TOPIC presence, not veracity: the authors coded stance separately and state that all 88 DPP videos were REFUTATIONS ('DPP-affiliated accounts disseminated 88 videos refuting such claims—accounting for more than half of the total voter fraud misinformation-related videos'). A wholly true item (a DPP news programme debunking the claim) therefore receives the label, so per §3 the row is coded QUALITY and borderline, i.e. kept but NOT usable as a prevalence-of-misinformation estimate.

estimates.date: Videos published 12 January - 1 February 2024 (2024 Taiwan election, held 13 January); videos and metadata retrieved in the last week of August 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of all videos uploaded by 94 party-aligned Taiwanese YouTube accounts during the election window that were coded as containing the voter-fraud narrative — SUPPORTING OR REFUTING it
estimates.value_raw: 170/5,641 (3.0%); by party DPP 88, TPP 44, KMT 24, Other 14 out of DPP 2,015, KMT 2,155, TPP 598, Other 873
estimates.denominator: 5,641 videos — every video uploaded between 12 Jan and 1 Feb 2024 by 94 YouTube accounts selected by the authors (16 traditional media groups from the NCC/Taiwan Periodical Literature registers plus snowball-sampled grassroots channels, balanced to 27 accounts each for DPP, KMT and TPP, plus 13 unaligned 'Other' accounts)
estimates.definition: A video was labelled voter-fraud if on-screen text, spoken audio, footage or implication carried the claim that ballots were stuffed, stolen or otherwise manipulated; videos whose only voter-fraud content was in viewer comments were excluded. Stance (supportive / refuting / neutral) was coded separately and is NOT part of this numerator.
estimates.misinfo_def: Misinformation is often defined as a piece of information that is not accurate or is misleading [76], which does not need to be created or spread with malicious intent (i.e., disinformation)
estimates.source_quote: Through this process, we identify a total of 170 videos as related to voter fraud.
estimates.page_loc: Section 3.2 Videos Annotation, Phase II, CSCW516:10; denominator in Section 3.1 and Table 2, CSCW516:8
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two-stage. Stage 1: an open-source LLM (LLaMA 3.1) flagged ballot-related videos from titles and VOSK-transcribed audio; validated against a 100-video human golden set (two coders, Fleiss's κ = 0.976) with Accuracy 0.910, Macro-F1 0.899, Precision 0.884, Recall 0.926. Stage 2: three authors manually coded the ballot-related videos against a written codebook (Appendix A.3.3), reliability on 100 randomly selected videos Fleiss's κ = 0.923, with collective adjudication for the most subjective rule. The underlying claim's falsity rests on the Taiwan FactCheck Center, which fact-checked and debunked the 2024 voter-fraud allegations, but TFC verdicts were not applied item by item.
estimates.moderator_quote: A video is labeled as voter-fraud on the basis of whether it contains the voter-fraud narrative (i.e., the claim that ballots were stuffed, stolen, or otherwise manipulated).
estimates.notes: DO NOT POOL AS A PREVALENCE ESTIMATE. The 170 mix videos that promote the false claim with videos that debunk it: 'Notably, DPP-affiliated accounts disseminated 88 videos refuting such claims—accounting for more than half of the total voter fraud misinformation-related videos.' The share that actually promotes the falsehood is therefore at most (170 - 88)/5,641 = 1.45%, but 82 is a cross-category sum I must not compute under R8, and the paper never prints a supportive-video total. Coded QUALITY + borderline per §3 ('If a wholly true item could receive the label, it is QUALITY'; 'When genuinely ambiguous → QUALITY and borderline=true'); construct OTHER would be equally defensible — what matters is that the row is excluded from prevalence. The percentage 3.0% is my exact part/whole from two verbatim counts with the same denominator (170/5,641 = 3.01%), permitted under R8. Denominator is a purposively constructed, party-balanced account list (27 accounts forced for each of DPP/KMT/TPP), so it is not representative of Taiwanese YouTube. Internal inconsistency to flag: the main text reports 2,771 ballot-related videos while Appendix A.3.2 says the reliability sample was drawn 'from the 2,421 ballot-related videos'; Table 6's column headers also appear misaligned with the values quoted in the main text (Accuracy 0.910 vs table 0.899).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Per-party voter-fraud counts (DPP 88, TPP 44, KMT 24, Other 14) against Table 2 denominators (DPP 2,015, KMT 2,155, TPP 598, Other 873) would give clean party-level shares, but they inherit the same supporting/refuting confound and would in the DPP case (88/2,015 = 4.4%) be a pure debunking rate; no rows created. (2) '2,771 ballot-related videos' out of 5,641 (49.1%) is topical relevance to ballots, not veracity — not a misinformation share. (3) 'We find 38 videos that fall into this category' (grassroots KMT/TPP videos presenting suspicious vote-counting scenes) is one of three supportive narrative strategies, with no denominator attached and no total for supportive videos, so it cannot be turned into a share. (4) Engagement medians (voter-fraud videos: views 12,558.50, likes 413, comments 76 vs non-voter-fraud 24,332 / 402 / 42) are medians, not shares, and the comparison set is a 3,667-video matched baseline rather than the full corpus. (5) Audiovisual medians (brightness, entropy, face rate, duration, loudness, tempo) and KS statistics are not prevalence quantities. (6) The stance codebook in Appendix A.3.3 defines supportive / refuting / neutral categories and lists refutation cues (R-2 'Official fact-check or debunk is cited', R-4 'Rebuttal to voter fraud supporters'), confirming that refutations sit inside the 170, but no counts per stance category are printed anywhere in the paper.

rob.design: Purposive/snowball account frame rather than a platform sample: 16 traditional media groups drawn from the NCC broadcast register and the Taiwan Periodical Literature newspaper list (excluding non-political and inactive outlets) plus grassroots channels found by Google-search snowballing, forced to 27 accounts per party for DPP, KMT and TPP with 13 unaligned 'Other' accounts (94 accounts total). Full census of the 5,641 videos those accounts uploaded 12 Jan - 1 Feb 2024, retrieved via the YouTube Data API v3 in late August 2024 (so videos deleted before then are missing). Two-stage annotation: LLaMA 3.1 ballot-relevance filter validated on 100 videos (human κ = 0.976; LLM accuracy 0.910), then three-author manual voter-fraud coding of the ballot-related videos with a written codebook (κ = 0.923 on 100 videos) and collective adjudication of the most subjective rule. Stance (supportive/refuting/neutral) was coded by two authors by consensus but never reported as counts. No confidence intervals; time window is 21 days around one election.
